question: For the parametric equations $$x=a(\theta+\sin\theta),\qquad y=a(1-\cos\theta),$$ find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of the parameter $\theta$.
explanation:
Differentiation with respect to $\theta$
$$\frac{dx}{d\theta}=a(1+\cos\theta),\qquad \frac{dy}{d\theta}=a\sin\theta.$$
Parametric derivative
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\frac{dy}{d\theta}}{\frac{dx}{d\theta}}=\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}.$$
Trigonometric simplification
Using $$\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}=\tan\frac{\theta}{2},$$ we obtain $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\tan\frac{\theta}{2}.$$
